sections.h2: What happens at the Recorder's counter in Steubenville?
sections.html:
This is where the permanent record is kept of each paper that moves land, secures a mortgage or adds some other charge on a Jefferson County parcel. The office is at 301 Market Street, Steubenville, OH 43952. A statewide legal aid directory shows it open weekdays, opening at 8:30 in the morning and closing at 4:30 in the afternoon. Ask for the current fee schedule before you go. The county's 2025 financial report counts five employees in the Recorder's office, so send complete packets and call ahead.

Jefferson County runs along the Ohio River and the West Virginia line, with Steubenville as seat and largest city. The county's financial report counts 14 townships inside its 410 square miles, with Columbiana County on the north and Belmont County on the south, as the report describes the area. Every parcel in the county is recorded here, whether it sits in Steubenville, in Toronto, the one other city, or out in a village or township. Property across the river in Brooke or Hancock County, West Virginia, falls under West Virginia's own recording system.

sections.h2: What goes into a recording fee on a Jefferson County deed?
sections.html:
Under R.C. 317.32 every charge pairs a recorder's base fee with an equal fee for the Ohio housing trust fund. Get the Recorder's total for your paper before writing a check. The statute's pieces are:

  • pages one and two: seventeen dollars to the recorder and seventeen to the trust fund
  • every later page, or fraction of a page, at legal size: four dollars and four dollars
  • each marginal reference entered by a separate instrument: two dollars and two dollars
  • a certified copy: one dollar and one dollar a page, with fifty cents and fifty cents more for the seal
  • an optional preservation surcharge, up to five dollars, that stays in the county's general fund

The surcharge entered the statute through Senate Bill 94, effective October 24, 2024. Only the Recorder can say whether Jefferson County charges it and how much.

sections.h2: Which conveyance charges does a Steubenville-area seller owe?
sections.html:
Two layers are collected at the Auditor's counter. The Auditor's own fee, in R.C. 319.54(G)(3), is the larger of one dollar or ten cents for each hundred dollars of value, fractions counted. Beyond it, a county may adopt a transfer tax under R.C. 322.02, limited to thirty cents on each hundred dollars.

In its 2025 annual financial report, Jefferson County refers to a four mill permissive conveyance fee and says one of those mills is dedicated to the GIS Fund by the commissioners. The Auditor is at 301 Market Street, P.O. Box 159, Steubenville, with phone (740) 283-8511 and fax (740) 283-8520. Confirm the rate with that office, since a permissive levy is set by commissioner resolution.

The seller pays, per R.C. 319.202(D). An exempt transfer travels with a statement of the exemption's basis instead of the fee.

sections.h2: Which family transfers in Jefferson County skip the conveyance fee?
sections.html:
About two dozen exemptions appear in R.C. 319.54(G)(3). These are the ones a family handling a house in the county is likely to meet:

  • a gift between husband and wife, or to a child from a parent, or to the spouse of either
  • a deed among the heirs or devisees of the same decedent, with no money paid
  • a deed into a trust that its maker can revoke at will
  • a deed that corrects or confirms one already of record
  • an interest worth one hundred dollars or less
  • a transfer by court order, except one that results from a sale under that order

A sale to an outside buyer is a different matter. Even a fast as-is sale for cash is a fee-paying transfer, and the seller covers the fee at closing.

sections.h2: How do Jefferson County housing figures compare?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 30,964 housing units for July 2025, with 70.5% occupied by their owners. Its 2020 to 2024 figures put a typical owner-occupied home at $127,800, monthly gross rent at $835 and household income at $59,055. Residents 65 and older make up 23.9% of the county, a bigger share than in Holmes, Huron or Jackson, and 17.7% of people are in poverty.

Census data show 27,143 households averaging 2.29 people, 3,559 veterans and 86.6% broadband adoption. The head count slid 2.5% from the 2020 base to July 2025, the steepest drop of the four counties. The Weirton-Steubenville metropolitan area, which adds Brooke and Hancock counties in West Virginia, is the labor market most residents work in.

sections.h2: In what order do the Auditor and Recorder act on a Jefferson County deed?
sections.html:
The Auditor is first in line. Any county transfer tax is owed by the grantor, payable to the auditor at delivery of the deed and ahead of presentation to the recorder (R.C. 322.02). The Auditor marks the fee amount on the deed, which then moves on to the Recorder.

Ohio gave county recorders, auditors and engineers until June 30, 2026 to provide electronic recording of conveyance papers (R.C. 317.13), and that deadline has gone by. A Steubenville title company can file a closing package electronically instead of carrying it across the floor. A seller handling a deed alone should bring the signed, notarized original if the office wants paper.

sections.h2: How did Steubenville and Jefferson County begin?
sections.html:
The United States built Fort Steuben in 1786 to protect surveyors mapping land west of the Ohio River. Settlers built homes around it, calling the place La Belle at first, and the town was later renamed Steubenville for the fort. La Belle was picked as county seat when the county was created. Through the first half of the 19th century Steubenville worked mainly as a port, while the rest of the county held small villages and farms. The county was organized on July 29, 1797, six years ahead of Ohio statehood, and reached its current boundaries in 1833 once Carroll County was formed.

Route 7 carries traffic north and south through the county, and U.S. Route 22 leads east toward Pittsburgh International Airport. About 408 square miles of land are bounded by Columbiana, Belmont, Carroll and Harrison counties and by West Virginia.

faqs.q: Which office records the deed on a house in Steubenville?
faqs.a: The Jefferson County Recorder, 301 Market Street. Steubenville lies inside Jefferson County, so its deeds are filed there.

faqs.q: Does Jefferson County charge the optional document preservation surcharge?
faqs.a: Ask the Recorder. R.C. 317.32 allows a surcharge of up to five dollars, and the office can tell you what it adds to a deed.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Jefferson County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. R.C. 319.202(D) assigns the Auditor's fee, and any Chapter 322 transfer tax the county levies, to the grantor.

faqs.q: Is a gift from a parent to a child exempt from the conveyance fee in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: Yes. Subdivision (d) of R.C. 319.54(G)(3) covers it. The deed still passes through the Auditor with an exemption statement before recording.

faqs.q: What is the four mill fee in the Jefferson County financial report?
faqs.a: It is the county's permissive conveyance fee. The 2025 report says the commissioners dedicated one mill of the four mill fee to the county's GIS Fund, which keeps the parcel maps current.
